items.title: FPL GW7 TRANSFER TIPS! | Top Picks Tier List for Gameweek 7 - 2026/27! ⭐
items.headline: João Pedro and Calafiori lead Gameweek 7 buying plans as Haaland becomes a Triple Captain contender
items.summary:
João Pedro is the standout forward buy for Gameweek 7 at £7.8m, combining strong underlying numbers, clinical finishing and a favourable enough fixture run to make a case for near-essential status. Erling Haaland is also a priority addition for managers without him ahead of Ipswich at home, with Triple Captain a viable consideration if he comes through Manchester City’s Champions League match unscathed. Dominic Calvert-Lewin is a strong longer-term option despite underwhelming returns: his three shots, 2.7 box shots and one big chance per game suggest goals should follow, while Leeds’ schedule improves markedly from Gameweek 10. Solanke is the more differential route, with penalties and appealing Spurs fixtures including Coventry, Chelsea and Crystal Palace.

Among current forward owners, Gonzalo, Calvert-Lewin and Thiago are holds because their chance volume and penalty duties support patience. Barry remains playable, including against Chelsea, after matching Haaland for shot volume and exceeding him for big chances, but poor finishing and bonus-point potential make him expendable rather than a buy. Wissa can be retained if already owned but is not worth buying at £6.3m because he plays too deeply, while injured forwards Alexander Isak, Igor Jesus and Brobbey should generally be sold to release funds and avoid uncertain absences.

Pascal Gross is the leading midfield buy at £6m. His penalty role, attacking involvement for Brighton and Crystal Palace fixture make him exceptional value, even if recent output exceeds the underlying data. Rogers is another premium-value midfielder with strong numbers and form, while Tavernier offers a longer-term Bournemouth route through penalties, set pieces and improving fixtures. Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard are holds rather than urgent purchases; Arsenal’s upcoming games against Forest, Everton and Hull offer upside, and Saka is an early captaincy candidate for Gameweek 10. Manchester City midfielders Cherki and Doku are attractive Ipswich punts only after Champions League minutes clarify their rotation risk.

At the back, Riccardo Calafiori is the premier target, with Arsenal clean-sheet potential, sustained attacking threat and a favourable Premier League role. Arsenal defensive cover remains a priority, with Gabriel a safe four-week hold and Konsa a cheaper short-term buy while his place lasts. Antonio Silva is the preferred medium-term differential: Bournemouth’s results have been poor but their defensive data is more respectable, while Silva combines set-piece goal threat with strong defensive-contribution potential ahead of Sunderland, Leeds and Ipswich. De Cuyper is an elite one-week Gameweek 7 option against Crystal Palace but carries major risks thereafter, with Liverpool and Manchester City next and Brighton winger returns potentially reducing his advanced role. Raya remains the best goalkeeper, while Petrovic is the recommended £4.5m long-term alternative; Pickford and Henderson are sell candidates due to difficult fixtures and weak team defences.
key_points: Captain Haaland against Ipswich in Gameweek 7, with Triple Captain in consideration if he avoids a damaging Champions League workload.
Buy João Pedro as the leading forward target; he offers strong underlying numbers, form and a manageable price at £7.8m.
Hold Saka for Arsenal’s improving run and consider him as a Gameweek 10 captaincy option.
Gross and Rogers are the preferred midfield additions, with Tavernier a longer-term differential on penalties and set pieces.
Buy Calafiori for Arsenal’s clean-sheet odds and attacking role, while Gabriel remains a safe hold and Konsa is a short-term budget option.
Antonio Silva is the preferred medium-to-long-term defensive differential because of set-piece threat, defensive contributions and Bournemouth’s fixture swing.
Treat De Cuyper as a Gameweek 7-only punt rather than a long-term transfer because Brighton face Liverpool and Manchester City next and his role may change.
Sell injured Isak, Igor Jesus and Brobbey; move on from Pedro Porro, Reece James and Tarkowski, while Pickford is expendable at £5.5m before Everton’s difficult run.

items.title: 13 things we've learned ahead of Gameweek 7 #fpl #fantasypremierleague #fpltips
items.headline: Erling Haaland is the standout Triple Captain play for Gameweek 7
items.summary:
Erling Haaland is the clear premium focus ahead of Gameweek 7, with Manchester City apparently unlikely to face any immediate disruption from their charges. If the Triple Captain chip is still available, this is rated an excellent week to use it on Haaland. Alternative chip opportunities include Hull at home in Gameweek 16, Bukayo Saka against Hull in Gameweek 10, or Bruno Fernandes against Coventry in Gameweek 14, but Haaland is the preferred immediate option.

Despite five blanks in six gameweeks, Bruno Fernandes remains a hold unless selling him directly funds a more important move. Morgan Rogers continues to offer reliable value after returning in five of the first six gameweeks, while João Pedro is fit again and is considered a strong forward option going forward. Savio also merits attention after playing 390 consecutive minutes; he impresses against Manchester United despite no attacking return. The goalkeeper referred to as Kyper has 53 points in six gameweeks and is still worth buying for managers with spare transfers.

There are several fitness and selection issues to monitor rather than react to immediately. Sosai misses Gameweek 6 with a tight hamstring but may not be absent for long, while Kevin Sharda picks up an injury against Aston Villa with no timescale yet known. Robinson and Mykolenko are also absent from their squads through injury, although neither is expected to be out for long. Vardial's benching after 490 minutes over the international break may simply be managed rest, but it creates some concern over his security of starts. Kza records DEFCON for the second time this season, a notable improvement on his Aston Villa output. Fulham disappoint again, yet their home fixture against Hull is enough reason to retain faith in Josh King and Gonzalo Garcia for now.
key_points: Triple Captain Erling Haaland in Gameweek 7 is the preferred chip play if it remains available.
Hold Bruno Fernandes through his poor run unless his sale is required to finance a stronger move.
João Pedro is back from injury and is a recommended option, while Morgan Rogers has returns in five of six gameweeks.
Savio has played 390 consecutive minutes and remains an encouraging pick despite blanking against Manchester United.
Monitor Sosai, Kevin Sharda, Robinson and Mykolenko for injury updates before selling.
Vardial's benching may be rest after heavy international-break minutes, but it raises a minor rotation concern.
Keep Josh King and Gonzalo Garcia for Fulham's home match against Hull despite the team's recent disappointment.

items.title: BEST SZOBOSZLAI REPLACEMENTS 🎯 | FPL EXPERT GW7 TEAM REVEAL ✅ | FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Pascal Gross is Tom Freeman’s priority Gameweek 7 replacement for Szoboszlai
items.summary:
Tom Freeman enters Gameweek 7 with four free transfers and £2.1m in the bank after a strong Wildcard in Gameweek 4. Erling Haaland remains the clear captaincy choice at home to Ipswich, while Cole Palmer is an untouchable premium despite a difficult trip to Everton. Freeman’s squad is generally well set up, but Dominik Szoboszlai becomes the pressing issue after a minor hamstring flag; even if fit, his limited attacking output makes him expendable.

The preferred move is Szoboszlai to Pascal Gross. Gross has three goals, five assists, 53 points and strong underlying numbers, including 11 shots and 18 chances created, while Brighton host Crystal Palace in Gameweek 7. His ownership is already extremely high around the leading ranks, so buying him is as much defensive protection as an attacking move. Brighton’s subsequent matches against Liverpool and Manchester City are not considered prohibitive either, given their form and capacity to score against strong opposition.

Freeman also seriously considers upgrading Barry to Joao Pedro, using the money in the bank to add a third Chelsea attacker alongside Palmer and Morgan Rogers. Chelsea’s run includes Everton, Tottenham, Manchester United, Sunderland and Leeds, and the absence of European football improves the appeal of their attackers. Barry and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall are still viable short-term holds, however, with Chelsea’s defence viewed as vulnerable and Everton’s later fixtures improving; Freeman can bench them for tougher matches such as Arsenal.

A Brighton defensive addition is another option, with Neco Williams a possible sale for a Brighton defender, but it is not essential. If Gross arrives, Freeman is likely to bench Ezri Konsa away to Nottingham Forest, while weighing up Kinsky versus Bart Verbruggen in goal. Other midfielders under consideration include Morgan Gibbs-White for Nottingham Forest’s upcoming Ipswich and Brentford fixtures, Aston Villa’s Manzambi ahead of a better Gameweek 9 run, and Bournemouth’s Tavernier, although European rotation and Bournemouth’s form temper that appeal. Arsenal assets Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard are earmarked more for Gameweek 10, when Arsenal host Hull and captaincy becomes more attractive.
key_points: Captain Erling Haaland at home to Ipswich in Gameweek 7, with Palmer retained as a premium cornerstone despite Everton away.
Sell Szoboszlai if his hamstring doubt persists; Gross is the leading replacement because of Brighton’s Crystal Palace fixture, penalties and elite chance-creation numbers.
A double move of Szoboszlai to Gross and Barry to Joao Pedro remains affordable, leaving £0.8m in the bank.
Joao Pedro is appealing as Chelsea begin a strong fixture run and have no European schedule, making a triple Chelsea attack feasible.
Neco Williams to a Brighton defender is an optional third transfer, but Freeman does not need to force the move with four free transfers available.
Bench Konsa away to Nottingham Forest if a Brighton defender arrives, with Morgan Rogers and the Chelsea attackers still playable despite their Everton meeting.
Delay a move for Saka or Odegaard until around Gameweek 10, when Arsenal’s home match against Hull offers a stronger captaincy opportunity.
Monitor Sharda’s shoulder issue, as a longer absence could make Brentford’s Anthony a low-owned differential with improved minutes on the left.

items.title: FPL PLAYERS TO BUY | GW7 ✅
items.headline: Erling Haaland is the standout Gameweek 7 captain, with Ipswich visit fuelling Triple Captain talk
items.summary:
Gameweek 7 brings a Saturday deadline and a busy European midweek for Arsenal, Manchester United, Liverpool, Aston Villa, Manchester City, Crystal Palace, Sunderland, Bournemouth and Brighton. Transfers are best left as late as possible where feasible, with Champions League and other fixtures likely to affect injuries and selection. Manchester City at home to Ipswich is the headline fixture, while Arsenal travel to Nottingham Forest, Tottenham host Coventry, Fulham host Hull, Brighton host Crystal Palace and Bournemouth host Sunderland.

Erling Haaland is the clear captaincy choice against Ipswich and is projected for one of the biggest scores of the season. Triple Captain is a viable play for managers still holding the chip, but Manchester City’s PSG match should be monitored first: Haaland may be rested or withdrawn early if the Ipswich game is comfortable, particularly with Semenyo able to cover at striker and Phil Foden back from suspension. Savio and Enzo are the preferred City midfield options rather than Cherki, whose minutes become less secure with Foden available. A Free Hit is not recommended, however, as the best projected XI does not offer enough of a one-week upside beyond a normal City triple-up.

Bournemouth offer one of the most appealing defensive routes. Despite conceding five in the previous round, they rank fourth for expected goals conceded after six matches and start a favourable run against Sunderland. Petrovic is rated the leading £4.5m goalkeeper buy, while Silva (£5.0m) and Truffert (£5.5m) combine clean-sheet potential with defensive-contribution upside; Truffert also carries attacking threat. Brighton’s Dipper is the top-scoring defender after another 15-point haul and faces Palace, whose defensive numbers remain the league’s worst, but his Liverpool and Manchester City fixtures immediately afterwards make Van Hecke (£4.9m) or Tottenham’s Vuskovic more durable alternatives. Vuskovic has returned in five of six matches and is viewed as a potential long-term hold. Gabriel should not be sold for Calafiori as an isolated move, unless the money is needed for a meaningful upgrade elsewhere.

Bukayo Saka remains a strong hold despite a frustrating blank, leading midfielders for expected goal involvement and retaining a major upside if Kai Havertz is fit enough to keep him on penalties. Gross is the standout value midfielder at £6.0m, with eight attacking returns in six games plus corners, free-kicks and penalties. Ta is another attractive £6.1m option for Sunderland at home, with Bournemouth also to come and temporary penalty responsibility. Chelsea’s Palmer, Rogers and Joao Pedro have combined for 19 attacking returns in 17 games, making a triple Chelsea attack worth considering, although skipping Palmer for Saka, Rogers and Joao Pedro is a credible way to spread funds. Joao Pedro is close to essential, while the lack of compelling forwards beyond him and Haaland makes a move towards 3-5-2 increasingly appealing.

For transfers, Joao Pedro is the priority forward target, especially for managers tired of being exposed to his ownership, though a Wissa-to-Pedro move can wait until Gameweek 8 if there is no urgent need. Gonzalo is a reasonable £6.1m punt because his underlying numbers are strong, but he needs to convert them after scoring only once from roughly 3.0 xG. Solanke has a good immediate fixture but is not favoured as a long-term buy. Gibbs-White should be benched rather than sold for Arsenal away if squad depth allows, as his recent blanks mask encouraging data and performances.
key_points: Captain Haaland against Ipswich; consider Triple Captain only after checking his PSG minutes and any rotation clues.
Delay Gameweek 7 transfers until after European matches where possible, with many leading clubs playing in midweek.
Petrovic, Silva and Truffert are leading Bournemouth targets as strong underlying defensive numbers meet a favourable fixture run.
Dipper is a strong short-term Brighton buy for Crystal Palace at home, but Van Hecke or Vuskovic offer better longer-term fixture security.
Keep Saka despite his blank, while Gross remains one of the best £6.0m midfielders because of set pieces, penalties and sustained returns.
Prioritise Joao Pedro up front and consider shifting to 3-5-2, with few attractive forwards beyond Pedro and Haaland.
Avoid buying Cherki now that Foden is available again; Savio and Enzo are the preferred Manchester City midfield options.
Save the Free Hit for a better opportunity, as Gameweek 7 does not produce a sufficiently distinctive one-week squad.

items.title: MY FPL GW7 TRANSFER PLANS 📝 Sell Saka to Palmer or Trust the Data? 📊 Fantasy Premier League 2026/27
items.headline: Haaland captains Gameweek 7 as Saka holds off Palmer and a transfer roll beckons
items.summary:
Erling Haaland is the Gameweek 7 captain at home to Ipswich, with João Pedro vice-captain, as the Wildcard squad is set up in a 4-3-3 and is expected to bank its one free transfer. David Raya remains the long-term goalkeeper despite Arsenal looking marginally less secure recently, while Brighton’s Maxim De Cuyper starts against Crystal Palace after his 15-point haul. The defence also includes Micky van de Ven for Coventry at home, Riccardo Calafiori and Lewis Hall, although Morgan Gibbs-White is a capable first substitute if any starter misses out.

The central midfield decision is Bukayo Saka over Cole Palmer. Saka’s non-penalty expected goal involvement for the season is cited at 0.69, well above Palmer’s 0.38, even though Saka was largely quiet against Leeds before missing a major late chance. Palmer returns eight points against Bournemouth but records only 0.07 xGI, no shots and no xG despite Chelsea scoring five, making his output look fortunate. João Pedro is viewed as Chelsea’s preferred captaincy option, reducing the need to spend heavily on Palmer; Morgan Rogers is considered better value than either premium midfielder. Saka-to-Palmer is therefore not a priority sideways move, though Palmer remains under consideration if Chelsea’s attacking output continues.

The immediate case for rolling is squad flexibility. Gibbs-White, despite facing Arsenal, offers strong bench cover for any position, and several potential future changes require two or three transfers rather than a single reactive move. Gonzalo García is retained for Fulham’s upcoming games against Hull and Coventry after missing two big chances, but he is on notice. Dominic Calvert-Lewin or Everton’s Thierno Barry are the likely replacements if García fails to deliver. Hall is also a planned medium-term sale, likely after Everton at home in Gameweek 9 and Fulham away.

Longer-term targets include Manchester City, whose home match with Ipswich appeals. Rayan Cherki is attractive after his Liverpool display and could be bought for Gibbs-White, but his minutes remain a major concern with competition returning and a Champions League match against PSG offering further selection clues. Bruno Fernandes looks overpriced for Manchester United; Bryan Mbeumo is preferred if he continues to play up front. In defence, a Brighton double-up involving De Cuyper and Luka Vušković is possible, although Vušković’s minutes may be affected when injured players return. Liverpool’s absentees, including Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai, should be monitored before selling, but Szoboszlai is not viewed as a reliable open-play FPL asset.
key_points: Captain Erling Haaland against Ipswich in Gameweek 7, with João Pedro as vice-captain.
Roll the free transfer unless midweek injury or rotation news forces action, with Gibbs-White providing first-bench cover.
Keep Bukayo Saka over Cole Palmer for now: Saka’s season-long non-penalty xGI is stronger, while Palmer produces no shots in Chelsea’s five-goal win over Bournemouth.
Hold Gonzalo García through Fulham’s Hull and Coventry fixtures, but consider Dominic Calvert-Lewin or Thierno Barry as replacements if he continues to miss chances.
Monitor Rayan Cherki after Manchester City’s PSG match; he is a high-upside Gibbs-White replacement but carries substantial minutes risk.
Bruno Fernandes is a sell candidate at his price, with Bryan Mbeumo the preferred Manchester United attacker if he remains central.
Lewis Hall is a likely future defensive sale after Gameweek 9, with Brighton, Leeds, Liverpool and Bournemouth defenders among the potential replacements.

items.title: FPL GW7 Early Thoughts 🔥 Sell Fernandes? 🤔
items.headline: Haaland Triple Captain call looms as Ipswich visit Manchester City in Gameweek 7
items.summary:
Erling Haaland at home to Ipswich is the leading Triple Captain opportunity of the first half of the season. The alternative standout Haaland fixture is Hull at home in Gameweek 16, but waiting carries the risk of injury, rotation or a change in form. Manchester City face PSG in midweek, so there is some chance of managed minutes, yet Haaland is still expected to start and can post a major score even in 70 minutes against Ipswich. Managers who want a differential chip route can instead consider Bukayo Saka against Hull in Gameweek 10 or Bruno Fernandes against Coventry in Gameweek 14.

Bruno Fernandes remains a hold despite just one return outside his Gameweek 2 haul against Ipswich. At £11.9m, his repeated blanks are frustrating, but Leeds away in Gameweek 7 and Bournemouth at home in Gameweek 8 are reasonable fixtures, while alternatives such as Cole Palmer and Saka are not clearly superior on a single-transfer swap. Selling Fernandes is most justified only when the funds are needed to restructure for Haaland. Saka is an even stronger hold: Arsenal face Forest away, Everton at home and Hull at home in Gameweeks 7, 8 and 10, and his underlying numbers and reliable minutes remain encouraging despite three blanks in four.

Dominik Szoboszlai is a wait-for-team-news decision after missing Gameweek 6 with a tight hamstring. Champions League squads and pre-match comments should clarify whether the issue is short term; he becomes a clearer sell if he is set to miss multiple matches, particularly with Arsenal ahead. Savio and Tavernier are the preferred replacements around £6.5m or below. Savio is a riskier Spurs punt but has strong upcoming fixtures after Chelsea away and appears likely to keep his place, while Tavernier offers good fixtures, strong underlying numbers and short-term penalty potential, although his recent early substitutions and European schedule are concerns.

Maxim De Cuyper remains an attractive attacking defender after his left-wing role and explosive start, but he is not essential for managers with a functioning defence. Brighton's Liverpool-away and Manchester City-away fixtures in Gameweeks 8 and 9 make him easier to bench than to start, and returning competition could eventually affect his minutes. Josko Gvardiol is worth holding for Ipswich at home if already owned, but is not a priority buy after being benched for Nico O'Reilly and overperforming his attacking data. With four free transfers, the current squad largely holds: the likeliest move is Sangare to a midfielder such as Savio or Tavernier, but rolling a transfer is viable because Szoboszlai can be covered and there is no compelling need to force out Gvardiol, Wissa or Lewis Hall.
key_points: Triple Captain Haaland against Ipswich at home in Gameweek 7 is the preferred play over waiting for Hull at home in Gameweek 16, subject to PSG midweek team news.
Keep Bruno Fernandes unless selling him is necessary to fund Haaland or another broader squad move; Leeds away in Gameweek 7 is still a playable fixture.
Hold Bukayo Saka through Arsenal's favourable Gameweeks 7, 8 and 10, with Hull at home in Gameweek 10 presenting a strong captaincy case.
Wait for Liverpool updates on Dominik Szoboszlai's hamstring before selling; he is more expendable if he misses Gameweeks 7 and 8.
Savio and Tavernier are leading sub-£6.5m Szoboszlai replacements, with Savio offering upside and Tavernier offering penalties and fixtures but possible minute risk.
Do not force a De Cuyper transfer if the defence is already solid; he is best bought by managers who need a defender and can bench him in Gameweeks 8 and 9.
Hold Gvardiol for Ipswich at home if owned, but avoid buying until his place ahead of Nico O'Reilly is clearer.
The current squad's main possible transfer is Sangare out for a midfielder, though banking a fifth free transfer is a viable conservative option.

items.title: GW6 Is Over... Here's What I'm Doing in GW7!
items.headline: De Cuyper’s 15-point haul tempts FPL managers, but Brighton’s fixture swing urges caution
items.summary:
Gameweek 6 produces a sharp split between De Cuyper owners, who collect 15 points, and those without him, while captaincy largely disappoints. Bukayo Saka, Bruno Fernandes, Morgan Gibbs-White and Erling Haaland all underwhelm as popular armband choices, whereas differential captains such as Pascal Gross, Cole Palmer, De Cuyper and Joao Pedro deliver. The recommendation is not to overreact to one volatile week, particularly with ranks still tightly packed and remaining fixtures capable of changing the picture.

Brighton assets are the central Gameweek 7 dilemma. Their home match against Crystal Palace looks attractive for attackers, especially Gross, but De Cuyper is less clear-cut despite his recent returns. He has one goal and two assists from just 0.84 xGI since Gameweek 2, with fewer than one shot per match over that period, so his attacking output appears difficult to sustain. Brighton also have Liverpool and Manchester City away immediately afterwards, while Palace continue to post strong attacking numbers and have just scored three against Nottingham Forest. De Cuyper is a strong one-week Free Hit pick, but buying him now for a longer spell carries clean-sheet and fixture risks.

Chelsea’s five-goal win over Bournemouth should not trigger a move for Henderson, whose two goals and assist come from only 0.12 xG and 0.05 xA. He is viewed as a low-minutes backup option whose explosive haul is not repeatable. By contrast, established Chelsea attackers remain appealing value despite an away trip to Everton, having again combined for 29 points in Gameweek 6. Crystal Palace’s combination of high xG and high xG conceded also strengthens the case for targeting them with Brighton attackers rather than relying on Brighton defenders.

Dominik Szoboszlai is a wait-and-see situation after missing Liverpool’s match with hamstring tightness following international duty. The issue does not sound serious and he is expected to have a chance of facing Brentford, so managers with a playable bench should hold. However, managers with several free transfers can consider a luxury midfield move. Manchester City’s trip to Ipswich is appealing, with Jérémy Doku and Rayan Cherki potential punts, but their minutes must be assessed after the PSG match because Ipswich falls between Champions League fixtures. Bournemouth defender Antonio Silva is another attractive target for his favourable run, set-piece threat and defensive-contribution potential, but he is a luxury rather than an urgent purchase for squads already covered by Arsenal, Tottenham and Newcastle defenders.
key_points: Avoid chasing Chelsea’s Henderson after his 18-point haul: his underlying output and likely role do not support another major return.
De Cuyper is attractive against Crystal Palace in Gameweek 7, but Brighton’s poor defensive data and subsequent Liverpool and Manchester City away fixtures make him a risky late buy.
Brighton attackers, particularly Pascal Gross, are more appealing than Brighton defenders against a Crystal Palace side that both scores and concedes freely.
Hold Dominik Szoboszlai if possible, as his hamstring issue is described as tightness rather than a serious injury and Liverpool face Brentford next.
Monitor Manchester City’s PSG minutes before considering Jérémy Doku or Rayan Cherki for Ipswich; rotation risk is significant with another Champions League match to follow.
Antonio Silva is the preferred Bournemouth defensive buy because of his attacking threat, defensive-contribution upside and favourable upcoming fixtures.
Do not make an early transfer: managers with strong squads and multiple free transfers can wait for injury, line-up and European-minutes information before taking a calculated luxury punt.

items.title: FPL Kneejerk Gameweek 7 🔥 Gvardiol BENCHED 😬 Szoboszlai injured 😭
items.headline: Dorgu’s left-wing role makes him the standout FPL buy despite Brighton’s tougher fixtures
items.summary:
Gameweek 6 leaves the squad on 76 points before Lewis Hall and Yoane Wissa play, with a green arrow from 131,000 to roughly 85,000 overall. Cole Palmer captaincy narrowly beats Erling Haaland, while João Pedro’s return arrives despite uncertainty over his Chelsea start. The immediate issues are Sosa’s tight hamstring, Sangaré’s continuing lack of starts and Josko Gvardiol’s benching against Liverpool, but none necessarily demands a rushed overhaul with four free transfers available.

Sangaré is the clearest sale: even when he produces defensive contributions, he is not getting reliable minutes and should either be moved on or left as third substitute. Sosa is more worth holding if the hamstring issue is short-term, particularly because there are no compelling cheap midfield replacements and a sale is only needed to finance a specific upgrade. Gvardiol is becoming a minutes risk after his Liverpool benching, although four 90-minute international appearances make a rest plausible; Ipswich at home in Gameweek 7 is enough reason to wait for Champions League team news before acting. Lewis Hall and Wissa are also holds for now, with Newcastle’s Villa, Palace and Everton run acceptable and Wissa still playing regular minutes and likely retaining penalties.

Dorgu is the major transfer target. Brighton’s defender is effectively playing at left wing and offers an unusually valuable out-of-position route into their attack; uncertainty over Kaoru Mitoma and Yankuba Minteh’s returns is not enough reason to ignore him while he keeps starting. Palace at home in Gameweek 7 is an immediate upside fixture, although Liverpool and Manchester City in the following two gameweeks may justify benching him rather than selling. Gross remains the preferred budget-midfield option even after his price rises, while alternatives such as Tavernier, Savio, Barnes, Enzo Le Fée and Yangel Herrera all carry compromises over minutes, fixtures or upside. Tavernier is attractive on penalties but Bournemouth’s European schedule and recent early substitutions create risk; Savio has started three straight 90s and has a favourable Spurs run, but is still not a standout pick.

Chelsea’s triple attack of Palmer, João Pedro and Rogers is viable against Everton because each is strong enough individually, rather than a problem simply because they play for the same side. João Pedro may also become the preferred Chelsea captain in Gameweek 8 against Tottenham if his goal threat outweighs Palmer’s penalty appeal. Arsenal coverage remains a priority through Riccardo Calafiori, Bukayo Saka and potentially David Raya or Gabriel, although Saka is chiefly a Gameweek 10 captaincy consideration against Hull and need not be forced in early. Haaland is the Gameweek 7 captain against Ipswich and is also a credible Triple Captain play, even with PSG beforehand, as 65-75 minutes could still be decisive. With few major fixture swings ahead, patience and saved transfers are preferred over forcing moves.
key_points: Sell or permanently bench Sangaré: his lack of starts makes him an unusable FPL asset despite occasional defensive-contribution points.
Hold Sosa if his hamstring problem is short-term, unless his sale directly funds a clearly superior midfield move.
Wait for Manchester City’s PSG lineup before deciding on Gvardiol; his Gameweek 7 home fixture against Ipswich supports a short-term hold.
Buy Dorgu if a defender transfer is needed, as Brighton’s defender is playing at left wing and faces Crystal Palace at home in Gameweek 7.
Gross remains the best-value cheap midfielder, while Tavernier and Savio are higher-risk alternatives because of minutes and team-context concerns.
Captain Haaland against Ipswich in Gameweek 7; he is also a reasonable Triple Captain candidate despite possible reduced minutes after PSG.
Keep Wissa and Lewis Hall for Newcastle’s upcoming Villa, Palace and Everton fixtures unless Wissa’s minutes fall against Coventry.
Do not force Saka in before Gameweek 10; retain the flexibility to target him for Arsenal’s Hull fixture and captaincy appeal.

items.title: BENCH BOOST ACTIVE! 🚨 | FPL CHAI'S GW7 TEAM SELECTION | FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Joao Pedro becomes the priority buy as Gameweek 7 Bench Boost plans face a Kevin Schade setback
items.summary:
Joao Pedro’s brace after returning straight to Chelsea’s starting XI makes him the standout regret from the Gameweek 6 wildcards. Both managers had expected a managed comeback following injury and selected alternatives to support a Gameweek 7 Bench Boost, but Pedro’s immediate impact confirms that he is close to essential when fit. The plan is now to find a route back to him for Gameweek 8, although Kevin Schade’s apparent shoulder injury may force an earlier transfer and potentially a points hit.

The wildcard squads remain committed to a Gameweek 7 Bench Boost despite disappointing returns. Josh’s team has Bernd Leno, Gabriel, Riccardo Calafiori, Pascal Gross, Bukayo Saka, Morgan Rogers, Kevin Schade, Gonzalo and Brighton’s Diego Coppola, with Lewis Hall, Harvey Barnes and Erling Haaland still to play in Gameweek 6. Coppola’s 15-point bench haul is particularly painful, while Saka misses a major late chance and Gabriel offers little set-piece threat in Arsenal’s draw. Calafiori, however, continues to look highly attacking and is viewed as a strong long-term pick despite Arsenal’s underwhelming form.

Fulham assets are a concern after a poor display, although Gonzalo misses clear chances and Leno is close to a clean sheet before conceding late. The view is that the short-term fixtures, especially Hull at home in Gameweek 7, justify keeping Gonzalo, Leno and Antonin Afen-Gruber through the Bench Boost, but Fulham players are likely to be sold soon afterwards. Brighton’s Coppola remains attractive even with tougher fixtures against Crystal Palace, Liverpool and Manchester City because he is playing on the left wing, is in strong form and carries both attacking and clean-sheet routes to points.

The main Bench Boost complication is Schade. Bournemouth’s Marcus Tavernier is the leading replacement at a similar price, with Sunderland’s Enzo Le Fée also under consideration because of penalties and a favourable run. Harvey Barnes is appealing as a player but less so for Newcastle’s Aston Villa fixture, while more speculative names such as Savinho, Pedro Neto and Eberechi Eze are discussed but not endorsed. The second wildcard team also backs Mohamed Kudus for Tottenham’s home match against Coventry, having been encouraged by Spurs’ performance despite their poor result, and expects Bournemouth forward Evanilson to remain a useful pick for Sunderland at home.

Both managers believe Gameweek 7 is still the best Bench Boost window because their squads are built for it and feature playable assets across Spurs, Fulham, Brighton, Arsenal and Bournemouth. The upside rests heavily on Tottenham and Fulham delivering clean sheets, while Gabriel needs to regain his normal set-piece role. The broader lesson is that spreading funds across a 15-man squad for an early Bench Boost creates a weaker group of premium attackers afterwards, making a successful chip return especially important.
key_points: Joao Pedro is the priority target for Gameweek 8 after starting immediately for Chelsea and scoring twice in Gameweek 6.
Kevin Schade is expected to miss Gameweek 7 with a shoulder injury, forcing a likely replacement before the Bench Boost.
Marcus Tavernier is the preferred Schade replacement around the same price, with Bournemouth hosting Sunderland in Gameweek 7.

Diego Coppola is worth keeping or buying despite Brighton’s difficult upcoming opponents because he is playing as a left winger and is producing attacking returns.
Gabriel is a longer-term hold rather than an immediate sell, but his reduced set-piece involvement and poor passing performance are concerns.
Riccardo Calafiori remains an elite Arsenal defensive pick due to his frequent presence in the opposition box, even if Arsenal’s clean sheets are not yet reliable.
Fulham assets are held for Hull at home in Gameweek 7, but Leno and Gonzalo are likely short-term Bench Boost picks rather than long-term holds.

items.title: FPL DEADLINE LIVE STREAM 🔴 FINAL TEAM! 🔒 Joao Pedro benched?
items.headline: Saka takes the armband as FPL managers weigh João Pedro risk after Chelsea odds plunge
items.summary:
Bukayo Saka becomes the preferred captain for Gameweek 6 after late concern around Chelsea’s attack. Chelsea’s projected goals fall sharply overnight, from roughly 2.1 to 1.9, prompting suspicion that team news may be influencing the betting market. That uncertainty particularly affects João Pedro, who returns from a knee issue and is photographed at training but is not clearly shown taking part in full team work. The final call is to move the captaincy from Cole Palmer to Saka, who has a favourable fixture and benefits from having been rested for England’s final international match.

The key transfer is Sander Sangaré to Josh King, with King brought in for Fulham’s run against the three promoted sides: Ipswich away, Hull at home and Coventry away. King’s underlying numbers are encouraging for his price, including a high volume of penalty-box touches, while Fulham’s short-term schedule offers a strong opportunity. The move also protects against a possible Sangaré price drop and retains flexibility to target Marcus Tavernier later, although Tavernier’s long-term data and set-piece role remain appealing.

João Pedro is benched after the King transfer, despite the substantial risk that he starts and punishes the decision against Bournemouth. The reasoning is not that there is confirmed Chelsea team news, but that the unusual odds movement creates enough doubt to avoid relying on a player just back from injury. The analysis recognises the alternative explanation: betting limits rise on matchday and heavier market activity can move prices without a lineup leak. Chelsea’s odds had also dropped before a previous match in which their major assets started, so the decision is a calculated gamble rather than a certainty.

At the back, Mendy starts ahead of Jurrien Timber/Konsa-style uncertainty around Arsenal defender Ben White’s counterpart Konsa, who carries fitness concerns after two separate issues and may be vulnerable to a late substitute appearance if Mosquera starts. Mendy offers a useful defensive-contribution floor, while Arsenal’s clean-sheet odds remain the best in the division. For wildcard squads, the preferred structure includes Saka, Erling Haaland, Morgan Rogers, Gibbs-White, King and Gonzalo, with Mohamed Salah-style premium alternatives avoided in favour of balance and a playable bench.
key_points: Captain Bukayo Saka over Cole Palmer after Chelsea’s projected goals drop sharply before Gameweek 6.
Transfer Sander Sangaré to Josh King for Fulham’s three-match run against Ipswich, Hull and Coventry.
Bench João Pedro despite his Bournemouth fixture because his post-injury availability is uncertain and the Chelsea market move raises concern.
Start Mendy over the doubtful Konsa, whose fitness and substitute risk make him less secure than usual.
Do not treat the Chelsea odds movement as confirmed team news: market limits and betting volume can also cause a sharp price change.
Gonzalo is the favoured Isak replacement for the next three gameweeks, aided by penalties and fixtures against promoted opposition.
For a wildcard, prioritise a balanced core of Haaland, Saka, Rogers, Gibbs-White, King and Gonzalo, with Mahamovic and a strong rotating defence.

items.headline: Saka captaincy wins out as Chelsea fitness doubts put João Pedro on alert
items.summary:
Bukayo Saka is the preferred captain for Gameweek 6, with Arsenal’s home fixture and his premium reliability outweighing the appeal of riskier alternatives. Bruno Fernandes would be the leading choice if owned, while Erling Haaland, Morgan Rogers and Morgan Gibbs-White remain viable alternatives in a highly split captaincy week. The key argument is that managers can gain a differential through a premium captain such as Saka rather than taking an unnecessary punt on lower-ceiling names such as Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall or Igor Thiago.

Chelsea uncertainty is the major late issue. Cole Palmer and João Pedro are reported to have trained, but a sharp fall in Chelsea’s market-implied goal projection, from 2.08 to around 1.91, suggests that an attacking absence or restriction may be circulating. João Pedro is the bigger concern and is not a captaincy option under any circumstances. He remains startable only when there is credible bench cover; managers with a strong alternative can bench him. Palmer is viewed as likelier to play and remains a hold rather than a priority sale.

The intended squad approach is conservative: roll the transfer rather than sell Palmer, João Pedro, Barry, Dominik Szoboszlai or Ezri Konsa for short-term moves. Konsa’s issue is an impact injury rather than a long-term problem, making him a strong hold beyond Gameweek 6, while Alex Scott is ruled out for several weeks and is a clearer sell. If an injured Alexander Isak must be replaced, Gonzalo García is the preferred short-term forward; Dominic Calvert-Lewin is a possible cheaper longer-term option for Leeds’ upcoming home-heavy run.

Defensively, Arsenal and Everton have the best clean-sheet prospects, but there are few compelling defender buys this week. Managers are advised to avoid forcing transfers and instead use playable budget defenders such as Bobby Thomas, O'Shea or Josh Egan where possible. Silva becomes a more attractive target from Gameweek 7. The late Arsenal leak confirms Konsa starts, but the initial uncertain report leads to Bobby Thomas being selected instead; it underlines the danger of making late changes based on unverified accounts.

Saka is ultimately captained, with Haaland, Palmer, João Pedro, Barry and the rest of the attacking core retained. João Pedro starts because of available cover, while Thomas is preferred over Konsa after the late uncertainty. The overall plan is to preserve flexibility for Gameweek 7 rather than spend transfers chasing this week’s fragmented captaincy and weak clean-sheet landscape.
key_points: Captain Saka in Gameweek 6; Bruno Fernandes is the preferred alternative if owned, with Haaland and Morgan Gibbs-White also credible options.
Do not captain João Pedro, as Chelsea’s falling goal projection raises concern that he may be absent, limited or benched.
Hold Cole Palmer unless a one-transfer switch to Saka strongly improves the squad; Palmer is considered more likely than João Pedro to start.
Roll transfers where possible rather than sell Konsa, Barry, Szoboszlai or João Pedro for short-term moves.
Konsa’s impact injury is not viewed as a long-term concern, but managers should use a playable defender if they are uncomfortable with the late fitness risk.
Alex Scott is ruled out for several weeks; Kevin Schade is a preferred replacement, while Isak can move to Gonzalo García if an immediate forward replacement is needed.
Avoid forcing defensive transfers in Gameweek 6, with Arsenal the standout clean-sheet option and Silva a more appealing buy from Gameweek 7.
Bobby Thomas is a useful budget starter, with strong defensive-contribution potential and notable shot volume for a defender.

items.title: FPL Gameweek 6 Deadline Stream 🚀 Palmer 🆚 Haaland (c)
items.headline: Palmer keeps captaincy as João Pedro fitness doubt drives Gameweek 6 caution
items.summary:
Cole Palmer remains the preferred captain for Gameweek 6, narrowly ahead of Erling Haaland, despite late uncertainty around Chelsea’s team news. Palmer trains after managing a recurring groin issue and is expected to start, while Haaland’s guaranteed 90 minutes and penalties make him the safer alternative away at Liverpool. Bukayo Saka and Bruno Fernandes are also strong captaincy options for managers who own them, but Martin Ødegaard is less appealing because he lacks penalties, does not dominate set pieces and can be substituted early.

João Pedro is the central selection dilemma. He misses Gameweek 5, withdraws from the Brazil squad with a knee issue and Chelsea manager Enzo Maresca says some returning players train more than others. That leaves a realistic possibility that Pedro is benched and receives a short substitute appearance rather than starting. Managers with credible attacking alternatives such as Josh King, Harvey Barnes, Kevin Schade, Antoine Semenyo or Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall are advised to start the more certain starter. However, Pedro is still worth retaining rather than selling in most cases, since he is likely to be back in the Chelsea XI by Gameweek 7 and has attractive upcoming fixtures.

The transfer approach is deliberately conservative. Rather than force a move from Vitaly Janelt/Sangaré-type budget midfield options solely to cover Pedro, it makes sense to roll where possible and carry four free transfers into Gameweek 7. Kevin Schade is attractive immediately because Brentford face Coventry and have no European rotation, while Marcus Tavernier is preferred as the stronger longer-term Bournemouth option despite Chelsea away this week; Bournemouth’s schedule improves substantially afterwards and Tavernier has short-term penalties. Pascal Groß is a good value midfielder but is not essential enough to justify selling premium assets or taking multiple transfers before difficult fixtures.

Managers considering a Wildcard should prioritise Arsenal defenders such as Riccardo Calafiori, captaincy options including Saka or Bruno Fernandes, and cheap active enablers such as Gonzalo García, King, Tavernier, Schade, Van Hecke, Egan-Riley or Afolayan/Gruber-type defenders. Avoid building a Wildcard around too many £4.0m defenders or injury-prone rotation risks. A Bench Boost is much better targeted at Gameweek 7 than Gameweek 6, with Fulham, Brighton and Brentford budget players offering stronger depth fixtures then.
key_points: Captain Palmer if comfortable with his fitness news; Haaland is the safer minutes-and-penalties fallback despite Liverpool away.
Bench João Pedro for a reliable attacking starter if possible, as he may be fit enough for a cameo without being ready to start.
Do not buy João Pedro this week amid the uncertainty; retain him if already owned because Gameweek 7 onwards looks more secure.
Schade is the preferred immediate cheap-midfield pick, while Tavernier is the preferred longer-term buy because Bournemouth’s fixture run improves after Chelsea away.
Roll transfers rather than making several moves simply to acquire Groß, Saka or Arsenal double defence; carrying four free transfers into Gameweek 7 is valuable.
If selling a cheap forward such as Calvert-Lewin or Isak, Gonzalo García is the preferred short-term replacement for the next three fixtures.
Use a Gameweek 7 Bench Boost rather than forcing one in Gameweek 6, especially if João Pedro or flagged defenders weaken the bench.
Avoid relying on unconfirmed lineup leaks for Aston Villa’s Ezri Konsa; if no reliable news arrives, do not make a panicked transfer.

items.headline: Bruno Fernandes leads a wide-open Gameweek 6 captaincy call as João Pedro remains a fitness risk
items.summary:
Gameweek 6 is dominated by late fitness calls rather than aggressive transfers. Ezri Konsa faces a late test before Arsenal's home match against Leeds, so owners should start him if they have adequate bench cover but prospective buyers should wait. João Pedro has only recently returned to Chelsea training after missing Brentford and is expected to make the squad against Bournemouth, yet a start and 90 minutes are not assured. Cole Palmer and Moisés Caicedo have trained for most of the week and are considered ready to start, making Palmer a far safer Chelsea captaincy option than João Pedro.

Bruno Fernandes is the leading captain pick at home to Tottenham, despite his low ownership and only one return so far this season. Palmer is the closest alternative against Bournemouth, while Erling Haaland remains a strong third choice at Liverpool because the hosts are without Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo. Bukayo Saka is slightly downgraded by Kai Havertz's likely absence against Leeds: if Viktor Gyökeres starts, he may take penalties. The captaincy field is unusually split, so managers can follow their own fixture or ownership preference, but Bruno, Palmer, Haaland and Saka are the stand-out candidates.

Liverpool's Isak and Gakpo are ruled out without a clear return date, so they are sellable unless a manager has a strong enough bench and wants to retain them long term. Manchester City receive positive news, with Haaland, O'Reilly and Semenyo available, while Liverpool's weakened attack improves the appeal of City defenders such as Joško Gvardiol. Manchester United are without Benjamin Šeško and Patrick Dorgu, potentially pushing Bryan Mbeumo into a central role against Spurs. Brighton remain without Kaoru Mitoma and Ma for several weeks, which protects Diego Gómez's minutes until at least the next international break.

For transfers and wildcard planning, Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya is viewed as the safest route into Arsenal's defence, while Riccardo Calafiori is the preferred affordable defender over uncertain options such as Jurrien Timber or Ben White. Lewis Hall appeals because Newcastle's midfield reinforcements and fixtures improve their clean-sheet and set-piece potential. Morgan Rogers is the leading midfield value pick, with his data and eye test strong enough to favour Rogers plus one of Saka or Palmer over forcing both premiums into a squad. Haaland remains the premium forward, Gonzalo García is a short-term option, and João Pedro becomes a leading buy from Gameweek 7 if his fitness is fully confirmed.

A wildcard squad should avoid overreacting to João Pedro's flag but should not rely on him as captain or assume a full match this week. The preferred current structure includes Raya, Calafiori, Rogers, Saka, Pascal Groß, Haaland and João Pedro, with budget changes likely needed to fund the final balance. A proposed move from Kevin Schade to Josh King creates an awkward selection dilemma because King, García, Groß and João Pedro would all demand starts; switching García to Dominic Calvert-Lewin solves it by providing a benchable third forward for Arsenal away. Haaland is the current captain in the working squad, with Saka vice-captain, unless late team news confirms Havertz or materially improves confidence in Palmer or João Pedro.

João Pedro is fit enough for Chelsea's Bournemouth squad but is not a secure starter or 90-minute player, so bench a nailed player with a good fixture ahead of him if possible.
Captain Bruno Fernandes against Tottenham if you own him; Palmer, Haaland and Saka form the main alternatives in a highly divided captaincy week.
Cole Palmer and Moisés Caicedo are ready to start for Chelsea, and Caicedo's return materially improves Chelsea's attacking outlook.
Sell injured Liverpool pair Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo unless you have a strong bench and specifically want to keep them for the longer term.
David Raya and Riccardo Calafiori are the preferred Arsenal defensive picks, while Lewis Hall is a strong short-term Newcastle option.
Morgan Rogers is the top midfield value pick, with Rogers plus one of Saka or Palmer preferred to sacrificing squad balance for both premiums.
